"""Build the one-page agenda for Eric's Thu 11/05 hour block with Kenny Boyd (Kenny look).

The hour follows up the 2026-10-28 Tech Sync: ARC (main item), the NCAA best-practices guide,
the technology inventory brief for Doug McNamee, and dates. Sources:
    ARC questions/dates  -> build_arc_docs.py (the 10-29 one-pager)
    NCAA positions       -> ../NCAA_BestPractices_Doc/docs/ssi-open-decisions-design.md (D1, D2, D4, D8, Q6)
    Tech brief           -> ../Tech_Inventory_Analysis/docs/STATUS.md (AD brief built 10-31; registry date 11/13)
Output: 04_Committee/Agenda_2026-11-05_KENNY_ER_<DATE>.docx (+ .pdf)
Run:  uv run --no-project --with python-docx python scripts/build_agenda_1105.py
"""
import sys

from build_arc_docs import KennyDoc, build  # same Kenny look, Word export and no-overwrite rule

DATE = "2026-11-03_v2"  # v1 lacked the "not penalized" line (Codex F4)


def agenda():
    d = KennyDoc("Agenda: Thursday, November 5", status="Draft for discussion")
    d.meta([["For", "Kenny Boyd"],
            ["Prepared by", "Eric Rash, Applied Performance"],
            ["Length", "One hour"]])

    d.section("The hour at a glance", numbered=False)
    d.table(["Time", "Topic", "What I need from you", "Handout"], [
        ["0:00-0:25", "Athletics Research Council (ARC)",
         "Answers to 5 questions; yes or no on the people and the outreach email",
         "ARC one-pager, request checklist, faculty list, email draft"],
        ["0:25-0:45", "NCAA best-practices guide",
         "Your read on the outline; 5 positions; 3 contacts; new dates", "Filled outline"],
        ["0:45-0:50", "Technology inventory brief", "When it goes to Doug McNamee. Proposed: to you Fri 11/13",
         "AD brief, 2 pages"],
        ["0:50-1:00", "Dates", "Confirm ARC dates (11/19 plan, 12/4 Schnitker, 12/11 approval); set our next check-in",
         "ARC one-pager"],
    ], widths=[0.8, 1.6, 2.4, 1.7])

    d.section("1. ARC (25 min)", numbered=False)
    d.para("The five questions on the ARC one-pager: members, authority, scope, first council "
           "date, and the name of the research and innovation lane.", space_after=1)
    d.para("People: three engineering faculty on the one-pager, plus a list beyond engineering "
           "(character, ethics, sleep). Outreach starts only after you agree to the names and the email.")

    d.section("2. NCAA best-practices guide (20 min)", numbered=False)
    d.para("My positions. Agree or change each:", space_after=1)
    d.numbered([
        "Form: the guide plus a one-page cover page. Together they are the department's "
        "standard operating procedure: the expected way of working, with departures noted, "
        "not penalized.",
        "Ownership: the athlete owns physiologic data. Baylor owns performance data, and the "
        "athlete can see it.",
        "Framework: the guide supplies the \"Version 1\" items of the Software and Technology "
        "Management Framework. Is the framework in force?",
        "Scope: the four NCAA SSI areas plus a short education section.",
        "Cover page: covers every unit that collects athlete data. You approve it. Athletic "
        "Medicine is named as the authority on physiologic data and return to play.",
    ])
    d.para("Also from you: a contact with decision authority in OGC, Procurement and ITS; where "
           "the May outside-counsel proposal stands; new draft dates, since the input requests "
           "to those offices and Athletic Medicine are not out yet.")

    return d


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(0 if build(agenda(), "04_Committee", f"Agenda_2026-11-05_KENNY_ER_{DATE}") else 1)

"""What the two document builders need from the machine they run on.

Both Eric's machines build these documents: the MacBook (~/DEV) and the Baylor
Windows laptop (~/Desktop/DEV). Everything platform-specific lives here so the
builders stay about the document.

  add_doc_style_to_path()  finds ~/DEV/Program/Baylor_Doc_Style on either machine
  export_date()            the date stamp of the newest raw/ export
  word_pdf()               PDF + page count from Word itself
  chrome_path()            headless Chrome, for the exec summary's HTML twin
"""

import datetime
import glob
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))


def add_doc_style_to_path():
    # Not a sibling of ROOT: inside a .claude/worktrees/ checkout there is none.
    home = os.path.expanduser("~")
    for c in (os.environ.get("BAYLOR_DOC_STYLE"),
              os.path.join(home, "DEV", "Program", "Baylor_Doc_Style"),
              os.path.join(home, "Desktop", "DEV", "Program", "Baylor_Doc_Style"),
              os.path.join(home, "DEV", "Baylor_Doc_Style"),
              os.path.join(home, "Desktop", "DEV", "Baylor_Doc_Style")):
        if c and os.path.isfile(os.path.join(c, "baylor_docstyle.py")):
            sys.path.insert(0, c)
            return c
    sys.exit("[error] Baylor_Doc_Style not found. Set BAYLOR_DOC_STYLE to its folder.")


def export_date():
    """Date of the newest raw export - the same file clean_inventory.py reads."""
    files = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(ROOT, "raw", "Quick_Inventory_export_*.xlsx")))
    if not files:
        sys.exit("[error] no raw/Quick_Inventory_export_*.xlsx found")
    m = re.search(r"(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})", os.path.basename(files[-1]))
    return datetime.date.fromisoformat(m.group(1))


def long_date(d):
    """September 15, 2026 - the style the 2026-09-01 documents settled on."""
    return "{} {}, {}".format(d.strftime("%B"), d.day, d.year)


def word_pdf(docx_path, pdf_path, timeout=180):
    """Export the PDF through Word and return Word's page count.

    Word is the authority: it is what the reader opens. None means Word could
    not be driven and the PDF was not refreshed.
    """
    docx_path, pdf_path = os.path.abspath(docx_path), os.path.abspath(pdf_path)
    if sys.platform == "darwin":
        # Word blocks on an invisible dialog if the app is not already open.
        cmd = ["osascript", "-e", '''
        tell application "Microsoft Word"
          open POSIX file "{docx}"
          set d to active document
          set n to (compute statistics d statistic statistic pages)
          save as d file name POSIX file "{pdf}" file format format PDF
          close d saving no
          return n
        end tell
        '''.format(docx=docx_path, pdf=pdf_path)]
        env = None
    elif sys.platform == "win32":
        # COM needs no open Word window. If Eric already has Word running, COM
        # attaches to it, so only quit when this build's document was the last.
        cmd = ["powershell.exe", "-NoProfile", "-NonInteractive", "-Command", r'''
        $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
        $w = New-Object -ComObject Word.Application
        $w.DisplayAlerts = 0
        $d = $w.Documents.Open($env:BUILD_DOCX, $false, $true)
        $n = $d.ComputeStatistics(2)
        $d.ExportAsFixedFormat($env:BUILD_PDF, 17)
        $d.Close(0)
        if ($w.Documents.Count -eq 0) { $w.Quit() }
        Write-Output $n
        ''']
        env = dict(os.environ, BUILD_DOCX=docx_path, BUILD_PDF=pdf_path)
    else:
        return None
    try:
        r = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True,
                           timeout=timeout, env=env)
    except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, FileNotFoundError):
        return None
    if r.returncode != 0:
        return None
    try:
        return int(r.stdout.strip().splitlines()[-1])
    except (ValueError, IndexError):
        return None


def chrome_path():
    for c in ("/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome",
              os.path.join(os.environ.get("PROGRAMFILES", ""), "Google", "Chrome",
                           "Application", "chrome.exe"),
              os.path.join(os.environ.get("LOCALAPPDATA", ""), "Google", "Chrome",
                           "Application", "chrome.exe")):
        if c and os.path.isfile(c):
            return c
    sys.exit("[error] Google Chrome not found for the HTML-twin PDF")


def drive_docs_dir():
    """Drive folder for the admin documents (SoftwareTechDocs/TechInventory_2026-08). Mac and Windows."""
    if sys.platform == "darwin":
        root = os.path.expanduser("~/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-eric.rash11@gmail.com/My Drive/00_Primary_Storage_Drive")
    elif sys.platform.startswith("win"):
        root = r"G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive"
    else:
        return os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "..", "deliverables")
    return os.path.join(root, "05_SYSTEMS", "SoftwareTechDocs", "TechInventory_2026-08")


def refuse_overwrite(stem, folder):
    """Stop before writing if a file with this name already exists, so delivered copies are never replaced."""
    clash = [os.path.join(folder, stem + ext) for ext in (".docx", ".pdf", ".html")
             if os.path.exists(os.path.join(folder, stem + ext))]
    if clash:
        sys.exit("[error] already exists, not overwritten: " + ", ".join(clash) + ". Move or rename it first.")

# Shell / Environment (macOS)

- **Terminal app: Ghostty** (Eric, 2026-11-02; `/Applications/Ghostty.app`, 1.4.0). Hand Eric commands to paste in Ghostty. To start a new Claude session or a long job in a window, run `~/.claude/scripts/new-session.sh <dir> <cmd> [args]` (e.g. `… ~/DEV/KeystoneOS claude "audit my AI OS"`): it opens Ghostty with the parent's CLAUDE* variables removed. A plain `open` from inside Claude Code passes them on, and the new session saves no transcript (Tier A `child-session-env-leak`). Exception: `com.keystone.clouddrivepush` stays on Terminal, because macOS grants Drive file access to Terminal (Tier A `cloud-push-launchd-blocked`).
- zsh/bash is the native surface on this machine. PowerShell 7 (`pwsh`, `/opt/homebrew/bin/pwsh`) is installed only to run the KeystoneOS `.ps1` jobs natively.
- **The tool-path list has one home: `~/.claude/TOOLPATHS.md`.** Read that file when you need a path. Only the traps below are kept, because acting on them wrongly is expensive.
- **Verify, don't trust any list.** `which -a <tool>` is authoritative. To read PATH honestly, scrub the environment first:
  `env -i HOME="$HOME" USER="$USER" TERM=xterm SHELL=/bin/zsh /bin/zsh -lic 'echo $PATH'`
- Traps:
  - Python is PEP 668-managed. Use venvs or `uv`, never `pip install` globally.
  - `uv` is a standalone install at `~/.local/bin/uv`, **not** Homebrew. Claude Code hooks call `$HOME/.local/bin/uv`; do not delete or relocate it.
  - `timeout` is NOT installed (no GNU coreutils). Don't use it in scripts.
  - Homebrew owns `/opt/homebrew/bin`. `/usr/local/bin` holds only app CLI links (`code`, `tailscale`); keep them, add nothing else.
  - Secrets live in the macOS Keychain, not in `~/.zshrc`.
- DEV projects live at `~/DEV` (not `~/Desktop/DEV`). Workspace map: `~/DEV/CLAUDE.md`.
- Primary storage drive (documents, data, deliverables): `~/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-eric.rash11@gmail.com/My Drive/00_Primary_Storage_Drive`.

  - SecondBrain vault: `~/SecondBrain` (Windows: `~/Desktop/SecondBrain`).

  - Printing-press CLIs: `~/go/bin/`.

Use the `gws` CLI (`/opt/homebrew/bin/gws`) as the default way to interact with Google services. Do not export its credentials or call Google APIs directly with tokens.

**Why:** Eric said so on 2026-10-22 ("use gws-cli as the default way to interact with google") after I tried to speed up Drive wave 2 by exporting the gws OAuth login and calling the Drive API over HTTPS; the auto-mode classifier also denied that.

**How to apply:** Script Google work as `gws <service> <resource> <method>` subprocess calls, parsing stdout only (stderr carries a keyring line). Each call takes about 2.5 s, and more threads do not help (4 and 12 threads both gave ~70 files/min on 10-22), so plan long jobs as overnight runs. Traps (2026-10-29): a download (`files get` with `"alt":"media"` and `-o <file>`) must land inside gws's working directory, or it fails with "outside the current directory": run gws with `cwd=` the target folder and a bare file name. Uploading new content to an existing file is `files update --upload <path> --upload-content-type <mime>`; compare the returned `md5Checksum` with the local `md5 -q`. Content search is `"q": "fullText contains '...'"` (~2 s, PDFs included); `drive_index.py find --inside` wraps it. **Never run gws without the login keychain** (`env -i`, a stripped env, a sandbox): gws 0.22 cannot unlock `~/.config/gws/credentials.enc`, deletes it, and every later call fails "No credentials" until Eric runs `gws auth login` in a browser (2026-11-02: one `env -i` test broke the backup's Drive receipt). A launchd job is fine; test a job's PATH with `env -i … /usr/bin/env node -v`, never a gws call. Related: [[drive-fuse-read-hang]], [[gws-forms-api]].

skills.name: codex-review
skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/codex-review

# Codex Review

Codex reviews; this Claude session coordinates. It runs each round, checks every finding against the source, records a disposition, and stops at the round cap. Started inside Codex instead: same-provider review is not independent, so follow `claudex-loop` with Claude as the reviewer: its `review` mode for a plan, `inspect` for code.

The invocation authorizes reviewing and revising the plan. Change code only when the user already authorized that work.

## 1. Set up

- `RUNNER=~/.claude/skills/claudex-loop/scripts/runner.py`, the installed sibling skill, never a file in the target repo. `python3 "$RUNNER" roles --host claude` must print `"reviewer": "codex"`.
- `S="$CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp/codex-review"` (or the session scratchpad), then `mkdir -p "$S"`. It must sit outside the reviewed checkout: the runner refuses artifacts inside it. `$S` holds the brief, dispositions and `artifacts/`; it is the run log.
- Pick the mode by what is reviewed:

| Reviewed | Mode | `--plan` | Extra | Next round |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A plan file | `review` | the plan | none | `--resume` the last result |
| A code change: diff, branch, PR | `inspect` | a brief in `$S`: goal, PR link, focus areas, what counts as correct | `--base` = the commit before the change | a fresh `inspect` |

  For `inspect`, run from a checkout of the change. The reviewer gets the diff of tracked and staged changes against `--base`, plus a list of untracked files to read; ignored files are left out. For `--base`, use `git merge-base HEAD origin/<default-branch>` for a branch or PR, `HEAD` for uncommitted work.
- `--model` and `--effort` are optional for a Codex reviewer: without them the runner's local patch uses `CODEX_REVIEW_MODEL` / `CODEX_REVIEW_EFFORT` (top of `runner.py`) and records them in `result.json` as `effective_model` / `effective_effort`. Pass them only when the user picks a different model or effort.

## 2. Run a round

```text
python3 "$RUNNER" review  --host claude --repo REPO --plan PLAN       --model M --effort E --artifacts "$S/artifacts" > "$S/roundN.out" 2>&1
python3 "$RUNNER" inspect --host claude --repo REPO --plan "$S/brief.md" --base BASE --model M --effort E --artifacts "$S/artifacts" > "$S/roundN.out" 2>&1
```

A round can take up to the 600 s default timeout: run it in the background and wait for the notification. The first line of `roundN.out` names the round's artifact folder; a first line starting `claudex-loop:` is an error from before the run started (missing path, missing `--base`, rejected `--resume`). Read the folder's `result.json`: `status` must be `completed`, then read `response.verdict`, `response.summary` and `response.findings`. Exit code 0 means a completed turn, not approval.

## 3. Arbitrate, then loop

- **APPROVED**: done. Present any low-severity advice and the reviewer's `limitations`.
- **REVISE**: verify each finding against the code or plan before acting. Accept and fix it, or reject it with a reason. Write the dispositions to `$S/roundN-dispositions.md`, then run the next round with `--feedback` that file:
  - plan: `review ... --resume <this round's result.json>`, same model and effort (the runner refuses a mismatch);
  - code: a fresh `inspect` with the same `--base`, after the fixes are in the checkout.
- **BLOCKED, `status: failed`, or a malformed result**: this is not approval. Report the missing evidence or the `error` field and `stderr.txt`, and fix the cause before spending another round.

Stop at 5 completed rounds, or the user's `rounds` / `MAX_ROUNDS`. A REVISE on the last round ends the loop: report its findings, and list any fix made after it as unreviewed. An approved plan that will be built next gets `python3 "$RUNNER" check --host claude --repo REPO --plan PLAN --approval <approved result.json>`; building and inspecting the result belongs to `claudex-loop`, because a plan approval does not cover the code built from it.

Flags, sandbox boundaries and result validation: [runtime reference](../claudex-loop/references/runtime.md).

**Done when** the last completed round is APPROVED, the round cap is reached, or a BLOCKED or failed round needs the user to fix its cause; and the report gives: each finding with its disposition, unresolved findings with Claude's position, rounds used, the final `result.json` path, and the model and effort passed next to any model `result.json` observed.

skills.name: meeting-prep
skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/meeting-prep

# Meeting Prep

Answers one question before the user walks into a room: **"Is everything I said I'd do actually reflected in the artifacts, and what do I need to raise?"**

The argument (or conversation context) names the project — e.g. FaceComps, RTP presentation, AppPerformance brief. If no project is named and none is obvious from context, ask which meeting this is for; that is the only question to ask.

## Step 1 — Reconstruct the "last agreed state"

Pull the most recent decisions about this project, cheapest source first:

1. Project memory files (`~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/`) and global `MEMORY.md` active threads.
2. The most recent SecondBrain meeting note(s) for the project. First grep the meeting notes for the line `- project/<PortfolioName>`, matching the name case-insensitively (written by `meeting-sync` step 4). Then also search for notes that mention the project, because untagged meetings are common: only about 2 in 3 project meetings get a tag. (the meeting-sync output in the vault — **Paths:** canonical vault locations live in `~/.claude/skills/_shared/config.<platform>.json`, e.g. `vault_inbox_meetings`; load it if unsure — if a literal path here ever disagrees, the config wins).
3. If still thin, `memsearch search "<project> decision" --top-k 5`.

Produce a short internal list: what was decided, what was promised, by when.

## Step 2 — Verify the artifacts match

For each decided/promised item, check the actual artifact — not the conversation:

- Open the current deliverable files (deck, PDF, calendar, spreadsheet, app) and confirm the agreed change is present.
- `git log --since="<last meeting date>"` in the project repo to see what actually shipped.
- Note any artifact that is stale, locked, or missing.

Mark each item ✅ implemented / ⚠️ partially / ❌ not reflected.

## Step 3 — The brief

Output one screen, in this order:

```
## Meeting Prep — <project> (<meeting date/person if known>)

**Bottom line:** ready / ready with caveats / gaps found

**Since last meeting:** <2-4 bullets of what changed/shipped>

**Decision check:**
✅ <decision> — in <file path>
❌ <decision> — NOT reflected; <where it should be>

**Bring up in the meeting:** <open questions, items awaiting their input>

**Deliverables & paths:** <every file they might present or reference, full paths>
```

## Rules

- Verify against files, never against memory of the conversation — the whole point is catching drift between "we decided" and "it's in the deck."
- If a gap is small and mechanical (a label, a date), offer to fix it now in one line — don't just report it.
- Do not restructure or "improve" deliverables uninvited; this is a readiness check, not an editing pass.
- Brevity is the deliverable: the user is reading this minutes before a meeting.

skills.name: dev-sync
skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/dev-sync

# DEV sync

GitHub (`erash11`, all private) is the transport between every place work happens: terminal
sessions on the Mac, desktop-app sessions on the Windows laptop, cloud sessions, Codex. The
session-end hook `~/.claude/hooks/session-autopush.js` pushes the one repo a session worked in;
it skips `~/.claude`, headless and cloud sessions, and any repo mid-merge. This skill catches
the rest: pull everything others pushed, push everything still local, keep both sides of every
conflict.

Eric pre-approves every operation here; run the steps straight through. Pause only when
something looks wrong: hundreds of changed files in one repo, or a large file about to be added.
On Windows, read [`PLATFORMS.md`](PLATFORMS.md) for the commands that differ.

**Guardrails.** Merge only: no rebase, no force-push. Anything in the way moves to a
`_to_delete/` or `_OLD_*` folder; deleting is Eric's call. DexaProject, and any repo whose
`CLAUDE.md` says its data stays local, is committed and never pushed.

## Step 0 — DEV root

Mac: `~/DEV`. Missing: stop and say so. Print the root on the first line of output.

## Step 1 — Config repos

In order: `~/.claude` (dotclaude), `~/.claude/skills` (claude-skills),
`~/.claude/global-memory` (claude-global-memory), `~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler` (code only:
`daily/` and `knowledge/` are gitignored), `~/SecondBrain` (the vault). The sweep covers only the
first three, and the autopush hook pushes only the repo a session ran in. For each: snapshot-commit local changes (Step 3.1
rule), `git pull --no-rebase`, `git push`. Then:

- **`~/.claude`:** if `machine.md` is missing, copy `machine.macos.md` to it. Run
  `bash ~/.claude/mods/mods-sync.sh`; report its line (`mods: N loaded, N disabled, N invalid`)
  and name any invalid mod.
- **skills:** `bash ~/.claude/skills/sync-to-codex.sh`, so Codex and Pi see the same skills.
- **global-memory** carries `USER.md`, `MEMORY.md` and the logs between machines, and the
  SessionStart hook already injected the pre-pull copy. If the pull brings commits, say how many
  and name the newest. On conflict in `transcripts/.errors.log` or `MEMORY.md`, keep both sides'
  lines: they are logs, and a dropped line is a lost memory.
- **SecondBrain:** the Mac's daily backup also commits and pushes it, at most once a day, and it
  skips a day on battery or a diverged branch; this step covers the rest.

## Step 2 — Inventory

1. `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py --sweep` (~4 s): every DEV repo two levels deep plus
   the config repos, one line per repo holding work not on GitHub. It reads local refs only, so
   repos that are *behind* show up in Step 3.2, not here. It already skips `_DRIVE` (the Drive
   mount: walking it hangs), `_ARCHIVE` and worktrees.
2. Missing locally: `gh repo list erash11 --limit 300 --no-archived --json name`, minus the
   folders `where-was-i.py --list` prints, minus `dotclaude`, `SecondBrain`, `claude-skills`,
   `claude-global-memory`, `claude-memory-compiler` (Step 1 syncs these five), `DEV`, `DexaProject`,
   `AppliedPerformance-Site` (local `Website/`), and `printing-press-library` (removed locally
   2026-10-23; cloning it brings back ~66,000 files).
3. Project folders with no `.git` (the DEV repo ignores them, so their work is tracked nowhere):
   check `~/DEV/*/`, `~/DEV/Football/*/`, `~/DEV/SpecialRequests/*/` and each Area folder
   (`~/DEV/Personal/*/`, `Program/*/`, `Research/*/`, `Performance/*/`, `Platform/*/`; the Area folder itself is
   a container, not a project), skipping `_*` and
   `docs` folders (the parent repo tracks `docs/`).
   `SpecialRequests/TOS_ES` is local on purpose (health data). Any other: list it for
   `new-project`.

Show all three before changing anything.

## Step 3 — Apply

1. **Snapshot.** Each repo the sweep marked `DIRTY`: read `git status --porcelain` first.
   Anything the `BLOCKED` list in `session-autopush.js` names (`.env`, keys, credentials,
   secrets, token files, databases, DEXA) or over 50 MB goes into `.gitignore`, or stays
   unstaged and is listed. Then `git add -A && git commit -m "<machine> snapshot before sync"`.
2. **Merge what others pushed**, every repo in one pass (~10 s):

   ```bash
   python3 ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py --list | tr '\n' '\0' | xargs -0 -P 8 -n 1 sh -c '
     git -C "$1" symbolic-ref -q HEAD >/dev/null && git -C "$1" rev-parse -q --verify "@{u}" >/dev/null || exit 0
     before=$(git -C "$1" rev-parse HEAD)
     git -C "$1" fetch -q && git -C "$1" merge -q --no-edit "@{u}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "FAIL $1"; exit 0; }
     [ "$before" = "$(git -C "$1" rev-parse HEAD)" ] || echo "PULLED $1"' _
   ```

   It skips detached checkouts and branches with no upstream. A `FAIL` repo with
   `.git/MERGE_HEAD` is a conflict: 3.3. Without it, the loop hid git's message: run
   `git -C <repo> fetch` and `git -C <repo> merge @{u}` by hand to read it (a fetch error, or
   local changes 3.1 left unstaged), and list the repo.
3. **Conflict.** Keep this machine's version and save the remote one beside it as
   `<file>.from-mac`, `<file>.from-windows` or `<file>.from-remote` (whoever pushed it), stage
   both, commit. Closeout uses these steps too. Exception: `transcripts/.errors.log` and
   `MEMORY.md` in global-memory keep both sides' lines in the one file (Step 1). `.DS_Store` conflicts: `git rm -q .DS_Store`.
   - Save the remote side by **moving** the file: a stdout redirect re-encodes the bytes.
     `git checkout --theirs -- <f> && mv <f> <f>.from-remote && git checkout --ours -- <f>`
   - While `.git/MERGE_HEAD` exists, stage only the paths you just resolved, by name:
     `git add -A` there commits the conflict markers themselves.
4. **Push** every repo the sweep marked `UNPUSHED`, plus every repo 3.1–3.3 committed in.
   `NO-UPSTREAM`: `git push -u origin <branch>`.
5. Missing locally: clone it where it belongs. Find the name in the area indexes
   (``grep -n '<name>/' ~/DEV/*.md``) and read its entry: a path written `Football/<name>/`, or a
   row under an "Inside Football/" heading, puts it in that parent folder; a project listed in
   PERSONAL, PROGRAM, RESEARCH, PERFORMANCE or PLATFORM.md whose header says its repos live in an Area folder goes
   to `~/DEV/<Area>/<name>` (check `dev_folder` in `~/DEV/project-triage/portfolio.json`); otherwise
   `~/DEV/<name>`. Then `gh repo clone erash11/<name> ~/DEV/<path>`. A wrong folder breaks the
   KeystoneOS paths and orphans the repo's Tier A memory (the slug is the absolute path). No remote:
   `gh repo create erash11/<name> --private --source=. --push`.

## Step 4 — Prove it and report

Re-run `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py --sweep`. For the two Step 1 repos it does not
cover (`claude-memory-compiler`, `SecondBrain`), run `git -C <repo> status --porcelain` and
`git -C <repo> log --branches --not --remotes --oneline`. Done when the sweep's last line reads
`0 need action`, both commands print nothing for both repos, and every problem left is in the
report with its reason.

```
DEV root: ~/DEV
Config: dotclaude, skills, global-memory, memory-compiler, SecondBrain pulled + pushed (global-memory: +N commits, newest "<msg>")
<mods line>
Pulled: <repos>    Pushed: <repos>    Cloned: <repos>    Created: <repos>
Conflicts: <every .from-* file created>, or none
<SWEEP line>. Clean. / Not clean: <repo: reason>, ...
```

## Gotchas

- **A push or fetch that hangs** is usually a keychain credential prompt: look for
  `git credential-osxkeychain get` in `ps`, and see
  `~/.claude/projects/-Users-kristinarash-DEV/memory/project_brew-git-keychain-hang.md`.
- **`cannot lock ref 'HEAD'`:** check `pgrep -fl git` first. If no git is running and the
  `.git/*.lock` file is zero bytes and older than the session, it is stale: move it aside, retry.

skills.content:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/startup

# Startup

The front door of a work session: sync, board, pick-up report, stop. "Sync" is what the machine
does (`dev-sync` owns it); "startup" is what Eric is doing. Global memory is already in context
from the SessionStart hook.

## Step 1 — Sync

Invoke the `dev-sync` skill and run it to its end. Done when its report is out and its last line
reads clean or names what is not.

## Step 2 — Board

The live board writes `portfolio.json`, so it starts only on a registry that already has every
other session's edits. Start it when project-triage came through Step 1 clean: no `FAIL` line for
it, no `.git/MERGE_HEAD`, and dev-sync's `Conflicts:` line names no `portfolio.json.from-*` file (an
older, committed one is a settled conflict). `board.py` finds its registry beside itself, so run it
by its path from any folder:

`python3 ~/DEV/project-triage/board.py --background` (Windows: the same file under the DEV root, with `python`)

It prints `board started at <url>` or `board already running at <url>`; put that line in the
report. Not clean: report `board: not started, project-triage pull unresolved` and name the
conflict.

## Step 3 — Pick up

Choose one repo, first match wins, and say which rule chose it:

1. The one Eric named.
2. **Deadline first.** An Active Thread in global `MEMORY.md` (already in context) with a date
   that is past or within 7 days: the repo its `→` pointer names. Nearest date wins.
3. The newest dated **project** row in `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py --days 3`. System
   repos are not picks: `~/DEV` itself, the `~/.claude` repos, `KeystoneOS`, `project-triage`,
   `drive-tools`, `_INBOX`, `TypeSafe_Sandbox`. Skip `uncommitted` rows too (that STATUS was never
   committed, often a broken repo).

Rule 3 alone kept a system day picking more system work (2026-10-17..31: ~75% of commits were
system). A status-report date (`~/DEV/WORKFLOW.md`, Biweekly) today or within 3 days goes on the
report's first line as `Status report due <date>: /status-report`, whatever the pick.

1. Read `<repo>/AGENTS.md` (or `CLAUDE.md`), then `<repo>/docs/STATUS.md`, then the newest file
   in `<repo>/docs/handoffs/` if it is under two weeks old.
2. A repo with real work and no `docs/STATUS.md` is invisible to every other session: say so.
3. `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/where-was-i.py --decisions --days 3` (`--days 7` after a longer
   gap): the open questions in each repo whose STATUS was committed in that window (each cut at
   220 characters; open the STATUS for the rest), plus the handoffs written. This
   keeps a multi-repo day from shrinking to one repo.

Report, after the dev-sync and board lines:

```
Status report due <date>: /status-report        (only when one is due within 3 days)
Picking up: <repo> (<rule: named | deadline <date> | newest project>)
Last session: <date>, <mac|windows|cloud>
Where things stand: <two lines from STATUS.md Current state>
Blocked on: <open questions, or "nothing">
Next: <top one or two from STATUS.md Next>

Decisions waiting on you (<N> in <M> repos):
- <repo>: <question, one line>
Handoffs since <date>: <repo/file>, ...
```

List decisions newest repo first, one line each, the question itself. Over about twelve: the

Started inside Codex instead: same-provider review is not independent, so follow `claudex-loop` with Claude as the reviewer: its `review` mode for a plan, `inspect` for code.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| A plan file | `review` | the plan | none | `--resume` the last result |
| A code change: diff, branch, PR | `inspect` | a brief in `$S`: goal, PR link, focus areas, what counts as correct | `--base` = the commit before the change | a fresh `inspect` |

  For `inspect`, run from a checkout of the change. The reviewer gets the diff of tracked and staged changes against `--base`, plus a list of untracked files to read; ignored files are left out. For `--base`, use `git merge-base HEAD origin/<default-branch>` for a branch or PR, `HEAD` for uncommitted work.
- `--model` and `--effort` are optional for a Codex reviewer: without them the runner's local patch uses `CODEX_REVIEW_MODEL` / `CODEX_REVIEW_EFFORT` (top of `runner.py`) and records them in `result.json` as `effective_model` / `effective_effort`. Pass them only when the user picks a different model or effort.

## 2. Run a round

```text
python3 "$RUNNER" review  --host claude --repo REPO --plan PLAN       --model M --effort E --artifacts "$S/artifacts" > "$S/roundN.out" 2>&1
python3 "$RUNNER" inspect --host claude --repo REPO --plan "$S/brief.md" --base BASE --model M --effort E --artifacts "$S/artifacts" > "$S/roundN.out" 2>&1
```

A round can take up to the 600 s default timeout: run it in the background and wait for the notification. The first line of `roundN.out` names the round's artifact folder; a first line starting `claudex-loop:` is an error from before the run started (missing path, missing `--base`, rejected `--resume`). - **A push or fetch that hangs** is usually a keychain credential prompt: look for

definition.name: mcp__claude_ai_Firecrawl__firecrawl_find_tools
definition.description: Browse Alexandria data providers and workflows or read a selected contract. Alexandria covers companies, people, jobs, finance and filings, public records and government spending, real estate, places and restaurants, retail and prices, package registries and developer data, news, research, and more: typed, sourced records through published contracts. Prefer normal firecrawl_search for a data task; it already returns matching providers. Use this tool when the contract you need was not returned in full, to browse a category when search found nothing, or before scraping the same fields from several pages. Discovery is free. Use query for semantic discovery or urls to find providers for a website. With no arguments, browse categories, then providers and tools. Contracts describe the inputs and outputs for execution through firecrawl_scrape. nextTool identifies further discovery or pagination. Discovery does not execute providers. Use firecrawl_search when you also need web results.

query.description: Semantic lookup of tools for the data you need. Selectors constrain the search.

providers.description: Values from each listed tool's `provider` field (e.g. "apps-apple-com"). Alone, lists that provider's compact tools; with capabilities, scopes them.

categories.description: Category IDs returned by an empty call. Lists providers by default.

groups.description: Optional group IDs for explicit group browsing.

capabilities.description: Values from each listed tool's `capability` field (e.g. "apps/app"). Put the provider in `providers`: {"providers": ["apps-apple-com"], "capabilities": ["apps/app"]}. A selected capability expands its complete contract by default.

level.description: Usually omit: it follows the arguments (tools for query, urls, providers, capabilities or groups; providers for categories; categories with none). Set providers or groups to list those within a category or url scope instead of tools. query, or a non-empty expand with any other argument, returns tools.

expand.description: Use ["options", "response"] for inputs and output shape without example payloads; [] keeps results compact. Omit for full contracts on selected capabilities.

includeCosts.description: Include per-capability credit prices (creditsCost, perRecord) in tool results.

objective.description: The user's underlying goal for this call, in one sentence: what they are ultimately trying to accomplish, not a restatement of the URL or query. Reuse it across related calls. Avoid sensitive information.

definition.name: mcp__claude_ai_Firecrawl__firecrawl_scrape
definition.description:
Scrape one URL and return its content, or execute catalogued Alexandria capabilities. URL mode returns markdown by default, or HTML, links, screenshots, branding data, a targeted answer, or JSON matching a supplied schema, plus page metadata. Firecrawl may serve recently indexed content; set `maxAge: 0` for a live fetch. A successful response does not by itself confirm the page is still current. A named browser profile loads saved session data without saving changes to it.

`firecrawl_search` with `sources` unset and `firecrawl_find_tools` can discover providers for the same fields across several pages; a matching Alexandria provider returns typed records in one call.

Alexandria mode: `alexandria` selects catalogued capability execution and is mutually exclusive with `url`. Alexandria execution is billed at the capability's listed price.

profile.description: Loads a saved browser profile without saving changes to it.

requestId.description: Idempotency key bound to one Alexandria execution payload. Generated when omitted and returned with the result.

alexandria.description: Catalogued Alexandria capability invocation, mutually exclusive with url. One {provider, capability, options} object or an array of 1-10, with contracts available through firecrawl_search or firecrawl_find_tools. Each call may include version to pin a published workflow; omitting it uses latest. Only requestId and timeout are supported alongside alexandria. The selected contract marks required inputs and any requiresOneOf groups (at least one member per group); it may include example.request/example.response and a key field under response (which may differ from records). Where pagination is declared, its fields govern paging with the same filters; catalogue next is separate from provider pagination. Returns per-capability results in data.alexandria with data, records, or an error with a code; individual capabilities can fail even when the outer response succeeds. Some providers require accepted terms; when a response reports a terms requirement, direct the user to the Firecrawl dashboard URL in that response.

capability.description: Capability address as returned by search or discover, e.g. "series/observations".

version.description: Optional published workflow version. Omit to use the latest version.

options.description: Capability options as declared by its contract.

definition.name: mcp__claude_ai_Firecrawl__firecrawl_search
definition.description:
Search web and specialized indexes, returning ranked results with query-relevant highlights. Each web result is a title, URL, and description. Operators include quoted phrases, `-term`, `site:host`, `inurl:term`, `intitle:term`, and `related:host`; the set is non-exhaustive. `includeDomains` and `excludeDomains` are mutually exclusive hostname filters; categories limit result types to `research`, `pdf`, `developer`, or `gov`.

For a programming question, add `categories: ["developer"]`. It searches an index of public repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, repository READMEs, and code documentation, and returns the results in `data.web` with `category: "developer"`.

For a legal or regulatory question, `categories: ["gov"]` returns results in `data.web` with `category: "gov"` and cannot be combined with other categories; `firecrawl_gov_search` is the dedicated tool. Verify gov results' issuer, jurisdiction, status, and version before citing current law.

Authenticated search combines web results, semantic tool summaries and domain matches. Use sources: ["alexandria"] for semantic tools only. Authenticated searches always add alexandria to the sources, so sources: ["web"] also returns providers; domainTools: false turns off website-matched tools only. Tool matches describe available structured-data capabilities, not executed data. toolDetail: "compact" (default) returns only provider, capability and description; "summary" adds metadata; "full" includes their input and output contracts. firecrawl_scrape with an alexandria body executes a selected capability; firecrawl_find_tools provides catalogue browsing and full contracts.

Returns result groups in `data` and an operation `id`.

toolDetail.description: Compact by default. Compact returns only provider, capability and description; full includes contracts. Inspect selected compact tools with firecrawl_find_tools providers and capabilities.

query.description: Query for web and semantic tool discovery. Operators include quoted phrases, `-term`, `site:host`, `inurl:term`, `intitle:term`, and `related:host`; the set is non-exhaustive. Catalogue browsing is available through firecrawl_find_tools.

domainTools.description: Include domain-matched tools for result URLs. Defaults to true when Alexandria is combined with web, news or images; semantic-only search leaves domain matching off.

highlights.description: Return query-relevant page excerpts for web and news results when available (default). Highlights appear in web `description` and news `snippet`; otherwise, original snippets are returned. Set to false to keep the original search snippets.

includeDomains.description: Hostnames to restrict results to. Mutually exclusive with excludeDomains.

excludeDomains.description: Hostnames to leave out of results. Mutually exclusive with includeDomains.

sources.description: Search sources; authenticated sessions default to web + alexandria, keyless sessions to web only. Authenticated searches always add alexandria to the sources, so sources: ["web"] also returns providers; domainTools: false turns off website-matched tools only. enterprise zdr or anon searches do not add it. Use ["alexandria"] alone for provider discovery without web results.

categories.description: Limit results to specific source types. `research` restricts ordinary web results to research-affiliated websites and returns page snippets, which is separate from the `firecrawl_research_*` tools that search paper abstracts and full text across biomedical (PubMed, bioRxiv, medRxiv) and arXiv literature; `pdf` searches PDF results; `developer` searches an index built for coding agents over public repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, repository READMEs, and code documentation; `gov` searches the Government Index of US federal, state, and local legal and regulatory sources, the index behind firecrawl_gov_search, and cannot be combined with other categories; gov hits can include historical versions, bill text, agency guidance, and third-party reproductions, so verify the issuer, jurisdiction, enacted/effective status, and version before citing current governing law, clarify a missing jurisdiction or ambiguous as-of date, and use general search for non-US questions or missing coverage (no hits does not establish that no applicable law exists). `developer` and `gov` return hits in `data.web` with `category` set to their name; the other categories also filter `data.web`.

objective.description: The user's underlying goal for this call, in one sentence: what they are ultimately trying to accomplish, not a restatement of the URL or query. Reuse it across related calls. Avoid sensitive information.

definition.name: mcp__claude_ai_Firecrawl__firecrawl_search_feedback
definition.description:
Records schema-validated quality feedback for a prior `firecrawl_search` UUID `searchId`. A `good` rating requires a valuable result or a valuable source, `partial` either of those or at least one `missingContent` entry, and `bad` at least one `missingContent` entry or a query suggestion; caps are 50 `valuableResults`, 50 `valuableSources`, and 20 `missingContent` entries.

Eligibility is limited to successful searches within the feedback age window. The record is idempotent per search ID. Eligible first feedback for a search can refund 1 credit; refunds are subject to the team's daily cap. The response reports whether a refund was applied, along with submission and daily-cap status.

Mark useful returned results in `valuableResults` as `{"source", "position"}` copied off the result. Groups are numbered from 1 independently, so `{"source":"web","position":1}` and `{"source":"news","position":1}` are different results. Be exhaustive — results you do not list are treated as not useful. Reserve `valuableSources` for useful URLs that were NOT among the returned results; never report one result in both fields.

valuableResults.description: Every result that was actually useful, copied from the `source` and `position` stamped on each result. Each group is numbered from 1 independently, so the source is required — `{"source":"web","position":1}` and `{"source":"news","position":1}` are different results. Be exhaustive — unlisted results are treated as not useful. Do not also list the same results in valuableSources.

missingContent.description: Array of specific pieces of content the agent expected to find but did not. One entry per distinct topic. Each entry has a short `topic` and optional longer `description`.

**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## claude.ai Firecrawl
Authenticated search combines web results, semantic tool summaries and domain matches. Use sources: ["alexandria"] for semantic tools only. Authenticated searches always add alexandria to the sources, so sources: ["web"] also returns providers; domainTools: false turns off website-matched tools only. Tool matches describe available structured-data capabilities, not executed data. toolDetail: "compact" (default) returns only provider, capability and description; "summary" adds metadata; "full" includes their input and output contracts. firecrawl_scrape with an alexandria body executes a selected capability; firecrawl_find_tools provides catalogue browsing and full contracts. Firecrawl provides web, developer, government, and research search, and executes catalogued Alexandria data providers. Use firecrawl_search to find relevant results across the web and specialized indexes; authenticated searches also return matching Alexandria providers in data.tools. firecrawl_find_tools provides catalogue browsing and provider contracts; firecrawl_scrape with an alexandria body executes a selected capability; firecrawl_scrape with a url retrieves one supplied page. For a programming question, firecrawl_developer_search searches indexed public repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, READMEs, and code documentation and returns the matched passages, and skills: "only" narrows it to agent-skill files; firecrawl_search with categories: ["developer"] reaches the same index beside ordinary web results, returning the hits in the web group rather than as passages and offering no skills filter. For a legal or regulatory question, firecrawl_gov_search searches primary law and regulatory material from US federal, state, and local government sources: statutes, regulations, codes, court opinions, and other government publications; firecrawl_search with categories: ["gov"] reaches the same sources in the web group and cannot be combined with other categories. For a biomedical, life-science, clinical, or arXiv literature question, the firecrawl_research_* tools search the paper index, while categories: ["research"] on firecrawl_search filters ordinary web results to research-affiliated websites. Use the firecrawl_research_* tools to search academic and research literature, expand from anchor papers via the citation graph, and read full-text passages from a specific paper. Search and discovery tools are read-only and return ranked results. firecrawl_search_feedback records a quality rating for a prior firecrawl_search by its id. Billing: web, developer, and research search are billed per request; government search is free; Alexandria discovery (firecrawl_search with sources ["alexandria"] alone, and firecrawl_find_tools) is free; firecrawl_scrape is billed, as a page retrieval in url mode or at each executed capability's listed price in alexandria mode.
